product: Rack-scale cloud and AI data center infrastructure: L10 and L11 server and rack integration, air-cooled and liquid-cooled, compute and storage. Showcases NVIDIA Vera Rubin and GB300 NVL72 platforms plus in-house liquid cooling and OCP storage.
demand: Hyperscale CSP AI and general-purpose server capex. August 2026 revenue of NT$144.3bn was up 50.4% YoY, the strongest month of 2026, and management states it is optimistic on long-term AI and data center growth.
pricing_power: Limited. As an ODM it earns gross margin of only about 7.5% to 9.3%; pricing power shows mainly through NRE income and negotiated business-model changes rather than unit price. Rising memory costs are being pushed back toward customers.
competition: Crowded ODM field: Quanta, Foxconn, Wistron, Inventec, Celestica, Jabil and Super Micro, plus Dell and HPE. Wiwynn is positioned as leading ASIC AI server ODM with AWS and is expanding its product and customer breadth.
team: Chair and Chief Strategy Officer Emily Hong; President and CEO William Lin; spokesperson Chen Chang-wei. Founded 2012-03-03, listed 2017-11-13, spun out of Wistron. Capital NT$5.608bn.
market_strategy: US onshoring plus global resilience: over US$1.6bn in Socorro El Paso Texas, over 2,500 staff next year and 4,000 at full capacity, second 476,000 sq ft building producing from Q2 2027, alongside Taiwan, Mexico, Malaysia and Czech sites. Push into rack integration, liquid cooling and one-stop AI data center, funded by US$942m H2 capex, a NT$15bn convertible bond and a US$1.5bn syndicated loan.
bull: Aug 2026 revenue NT$144.3bn +50.4% YoY, Q2 PAT +23.5%, Texas plant opened 2026-09-14, AWS named customer; FactSet 2026 EPS about NT$121 rising to NT$183 in 2027.
bear: Gross margin only 7.5-9.3% and pressured by memory costs; Q2 growth slowed to +26.0% from H1 +41.7%; all 18 analysts bullish, no dissent; stock 26% below 2026-09-01 high despite notes.
falsifier: Q3 2026 results (TWSE filing deadline 2026-11-14) showing gross margin below 7.5% or revenue growth below 26% YoY.

web_what_changed: Aug 7 2026 Q2: revenue NT$278.153bn +26.0% YoY, PAT NT$14.969bn +23.5%, GM 9.3%, EPS NT$80.43 pre-split; H1 revenue NT$554.660bn +41.7%. Sept 2 ex-rights stock dividend, a 1-for-3 split (1 share became 3, about 66% EPS restatement). Sept 14-15 Texas Socorro plant opened, over US$1.6bn invested. Aug revenue NT$144.3bn +50.4% YoY.
web_not_known_yesterday: Not found. No company disclosure dated 2026-09-24 or 2026-09-25 was located. Most recent dated item is the 2026-09-21 Goldman Sachs note raising the price target to NT$3,777 (post-split basis, over NT$10,000 pre-split) on strong August revenue.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Growth is mostly AI and ASIC server volume plus mix shift to rack-scale AI, with added general-purpose server restock by US CSPs. Reported revenue is distorted because from April 2026 memory procurement for some customers moved to an agency model, excluding those amounts from revenue and cost. Some pricing effect comes from NRE income and customer business-model adjustments amid rising memory costs.
web_suppliers: NVIDIA and AMD GPUs and CPUs, AWS Annapurna Labs ASICs, Intel platforms. Memory DRAM and HBM is the binding constraint: Q2 release cites rising component costs and a shift to a procurement agency model. Liquid-cooling partner Shinwa Controls, co-packaged optics with Ayar Labs, and GUC for silicon-to-system. Power infrastructure is the other named bottleneck behind the US$942m H2 2026 capex.
web_customers: Highly concentrated in a few US hyperscalers. Amazon AWS is a named dominant customer: Amazon and Wiwynn jointly announced the Socorro Texas expansion on 2026-09-10, and Amazon Annapurna Labs executives spoke at the 2026-09-14 opening. Microsoft is also referenced as an attending CSP and past immersion-cooling partner. Exact customer revenue shares are not disclosed by the company.
web_who_loses: Rival cloud-server ODMs and EMS: Quanta, Foxconn Hon Hai, Wistron, Inventec, Celestica, Jabil and Super Micro, plus Dell and HPE in AI server share. Buyers of merchant GPU servers lose to ASIC-based rack designs. Wistron loses relative standing as Wiwynn becomes the group AI leader.
web_contradicting_evidence: Gross margin is thin at 7.5-9.3% and pressured by memory cost inflation; Q2 revenue growth slowed to +26.0% versus H1 +41.7%. The stock sits about 26% below its 52-week high of NT$2,875 set 2026-09-01, despite bullish notes. All 18 tracked analysts are bullish, so consensus is crowded with no dissent. H2 capex of US$942m plus a NT$15bn convertible bond and US$1.5bn syndicated loan raise dilution and leverage risk.
web_if_management_right: AI and ASIC rack demand persists, Texas and global capacity converts to revenue, and 2026 revenue approaches NT$1.3 trillion. FactSet post-split 2026 EPS consensus is about NT$121 rising toward NT$183 in 2027. Sell-side consensus mean target of NT$2,785 implies roughly 32% upside from NT$2,115.
web_if_management_wrong: Margin and cash break first. Memory and component cost inflation plus US onshoring costs compress gross margin from 9.3%, while working capital, the US$942m capex, the NT$15bn convertible and the US$1.5bn syndicated loan bite simultaneously. A single-customer demand pause then hits revenue and EPS together.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: Liquid-cooling and thermal suppliers including Shinwa Controls and Taiwan cooling makers, power and PSU and BBU vendors, co-packaged optics via Ayar Labs, ASIC design services around GUC, and the Taiwan, Mexico, Malaysia and Czech component and rack-integration cluster.
